name: Jean-Claude Passeron
evidence: SUDOC record: 'Les mots de la sociologie / texte original soumis au jury pour la soutenance du doctorat d'Etat par Jean-Claude Passeron ; sous la direction de Michel Verret', 1980.
notes: Thèse d'État, Nantes sociology dept, March 1980 (fr.wikipedia confirms 1980 thèse d'État 'Les mots de la sociologie'). Record found on Verret's Persée authority page (SUDOC-derived). Agrégé de philosophie 1958; long-time Bourdieu collaborator, but Bourdieu was not his thesis director.

name: Howard Schuman
evidence: Wikipedia: PhD sociology, Harvard 1961, dissertation 'Social structure and personality constriction in a total institution'; no advisor named.
notes: Wikidata has no P184. A biographical entry mentions work at Harvard with Gordon Allport and later project with Alex Inkeles (1962-64); neither stated as dissertation advisor. ProQuest record would settle it.

name: Herbert H. Hyman
evidence: Wikipedia: Columbia PhD 1942, thesis 'The psychology of status'; no advisor named.
notes: PhD in social psychology (Columbia finding aid). Sheatsley POQ memoriam (1986) paywalled; not checked. Do not infer Murphy/Klineberg without a source.

name: François Alphonse Aulard
evidence: Doctorat ès lettres, Paris 1877; theses on Leopardi and Asinius Pollio defended 22 June 1877; record names only a report by Mézières, no director.
notes: 19th-century doctorat ès lettres had no formal thesis director; Alfred Mézières wrote the soutenance report (rapporteur/jury role, not supervisor). Reviewer may prefer not_found if strictness required.

name: Jean-Daniel Reynaud
evidence: Normalien, agrégé de philosophie 1946, CNRS 1950 at Friedmann's Centre d'études sociologiques; no doctorate or thesis director mentioned.
notes: Unclear whether he ever defended a doctorate (Persée/IdRef list only theses he directed). Georges Friedmann was his patron and Cnam predecessor, not documented as thesis director. Could be no_doctoral_advisor if a source confirms no doctorate.

name: Michel Offerlé
evidence: SUDOC record: 'Les socialistes et Paris : 1881-1900 : des Communards aux conseillers municipaux / par Michel Offerlé ; sous la direction de Marcel David', 1979.
notes: Doctorat d'État en science politique, Paris 1, 1979 (fr.wikipedia). A HAL article also describes Marcel David (historian of law/labour, 1920-2011) as his thesis director.

name: Albert Aftalion
evidence: Two doctoral theses before the Paris law faculty: legal sciences (May 1898) and economics, 'L'œuvre économique de Simonde de Sismondi' (June 1899); no supervisor named.
notes: Paris law-faculty doctorates of the 1890s had a jury president rather than a supervisor; none named in sources found. Reviewer may downgrade to not_found.

name: Jean Duvignaud
evidence: 'devient assistant de Georges Gurvitch à la Sorbonne, sous la direction duquel il soutient en 1965 sa thèse d'état sur le théâtre'
notes: Thèse d'État published as 'Sociologie du théâtre' (PUF 1965), complementary thesis 'L'acteur'. Single source names the director.

name: François Chazel
evidence: Universalis: long stay at Harvard with Parsons 'qui déboucha sur une thèse d'État sous la direction de Stoetzel'.
notes: Thesis published 1974 as 'La théorie analytique de la société dans l'œuvre de Talcott Parsons'; Livres Hebdo gives defense 1972. Parsons was a host at Harvard, not the director. Institution inferred (Stoetzel at Sorbonne); single source for director.

name: Dominique Martin
evidence: Persée/theses.fr list theses he directed (Vrancken 1993, Monchatre 1996, Berthelot 2005, Lecaplain 2012) but not his own thesis.
notes: Identity confirmed: sociologist of work, MCF at IEP Paris, later Rennes 2, Grenoble 2, Lyon 2; students match known_students. Own doctorate not located.

name: Émile Sicard
evidence: IdRef note: 'Auteur d'une thèse en sociologie à Clermont-Ferrand en 1942' (La Zadruga sud-slave..., publ. 1943); no director named.
notes: Doctorat ès lettres (thèse d'État era) at Clermont-Ferrand (Strasbourg faculty in exile during WWII). Possibly no named director; no source states one.

name: Henri Desroche
evidence: Thèse d'État, soutenue en 1970, 'Messianismes, utopies et sociologie des religions'; no director named.
notes: Close to Gabriel Le Bras (Groupe de sociologie des religions founded under Le Bras's aegis), but no source names Le Bras as thesis director. Do not infer.

name: Robert Castel
evidence: 'Ces recherches aboutiront à une thèse d'État ès lettres et sciences humaines, sous la direction d'Aron, soutenue en 1980.'
notes: Wikipedia FR; institution not stated. Universalis loosely links the thesis to L'Ordre psychiatrique (1976); defense year per Wikipedia 1980.

name: Jean Séguy
evidence: Thèse d'État 'Les assemblées anabaptistes-mennonites de France', 1970; no director named.
notes: Reviews call it a doctorat ès lettres at the Sorbonne, June 1970. Hervieu-Léger's 2008 ASSR memoriam not accessed; may name director.

name: Angus Campbell
evidence: Wikipedia infobox: doctoral advisor Ernest Hilgard; thesis 'An Experimental Analysis of Ease of Conditioning in Man' (1936); doctoral student Philip Converse.
notes: Search summaries indicate American National Biography and Encyclopedia.com also name Hilgard (not directly verified). Converse matches known_students.

name: Jean-Claude Chamboredon
evidence: Archive fonds lists a 'Projet de thèse de doctorat d'État, « Socialisation primaire et socialisation secondaire »'; no defense or director recorded.
notes: Normalien 1959, agrégé de lettres classiques 1962; possibly never defended a doctorate (career at ENS/EHESS). No source confirms either way; not to be attributed to Bourdieu.

name: George Eaton Simpson
evidence: 'The Negro in the Philadelphia Press: A Dissertation in Sociology Presented to the Faculty of the Graduate School of the University of Pennsylvania' (publ. 1936); no advisor named.
notes: Identity: anthropologist/sociologist, Temple, Penn State, Oberlin. Book front matter might name adviser; not accessible.

name: Henri Mendras
evidence: Doctorat d'État; thèse principale 'Les transformations du métier d'agriculteur dans la France contemporaine' (1967); no director named.
notes: Wikipedia FR: inspired by Gurvitch and Friedmann; studied at Chicago. Neither stated as director.

name: Gresham Sykes
evidence: Britannica: studied sociology at Northwestern University (Ph.D., 1954); no advisor named.
notes: PhD year conflicts (1952 ASA obit, 1953 Prabook, 1954 Britannica/Heiner tribute). Society of Captives acknowledges Cressey, Grosser, Hartung, McCleery, Ohlin - not an advisor statement.

name: Torgny T. Segerstedt
evidence: SBL: doctor and docent in practical philosophy at Lund 1934; dissertation 'Value and reality in Bradley's philosophy', largely finished in London; no supervisor named.
notes: Teachers mentioned: Efraim Liljeqvist (professor), Gunnar Aspelin; neither described as supervisor. Swedish disputations of the era rarely name a formal handledare.

name: Michel Simon
evidence: Maitron: he was working on a thèse de doctorat d'État under the direction of Raymond Aron, on the sociology of socialist militants and their class membership.
notes: Maitron describes thesis in preparation under Aron; Babelio says 'Docteur ès lettres et sciences humaines'. Defense year/title not verified (one search summary claimed 1977 'Contributions à une sociologie du comportement politique' - unconfirmed). Maitron page blocked to direct fetch; quote taken from search snippet. Identity: Lille 1 Institut de sociologie, Clersé founder.

name: William G. Tierney
evidence: Ph.D. from Stanford in administration and policy analysis (CV: 1984, with M.A. anthropology); no advisor named.
notes: USC CV PDFs blocked (401). Dissertation record via ProQuest/Stanford SearchWorks would settle it.

name: Michel Crozier
evidence: CSO: 'Docteur en droit' and 'Docteur d'Etat ès Lettres'; Le Phénomène bureaucratique written 'sous forme de thèse d'État'; no director named.
notes: Two doctorates: law doctorate (1949, thesis on American unionism) and thèse d'État (Sorbonne, 1964). Aron and Friedmann reportedly sat on/commented at the 1964 defense, but neither named as director.

name: Yves Goussault
evidence: SUDOC: 'Crise et réforme des structures agraires : le cas chilien et ses applications méthodologiques / Yves Goussault ; sous la direction de Pierre George', 1972.
notes: Thèse d'État; Paris 1 catalogue files it under Géographie, dated 20/12/1972 (Maitron says 1973). Pierre George was a geographer.

name: Peter Conrad
evidence: Ph.D. in sociology from Boston University in 1976; dissertation became 'Identifying Hyperactive Children'; no advisor named.
notes: Brandeis CV and memorial PDF blocked (403). Irving Zola was a collaborator; no evidence he was the advisor - do not infer.
